why: The must_catch item says "Line 2" should FAIL as ambiguous, with two readings named. Counting from 0, line 2 is "average handles bad input sensibly". That is the only vague line. The second line, read 1-based, gives exact inputs and outputs and can't be read as ambiguous, so I took the item to mean the bad-input line. The output marks that line "FAIL". It says the words fix neither which inputs count as bad nor what "sensibly" means. It names two readings: "Build A throws TypeError on average(null)" and "Build B returns 0 for null", and says "Two careful readers will disagree." The wrong_build section makes the same point: the opposite build "also 'meets' line 3 for another reader." So the trap is caught. If "Line 2" was meant 1-based, this would be false, because the output passes that line.
